description: A genome model produces a viable design for an organism able to infect humans, or a credible study shows a non-expert reaching that point with model assistance. It is contested on methodology, the authors are accused of both alarmism and of publishing a recipe, and the argument stays inside the biosecurity community – but it is a categorically stronger signal than anything published so far. This is a precursor: it opens the bio gate for the next 4 turns.

Benchmark results from an unreleased system leak, or an evaluation team reports behaviour it cannot explain – capability appearing where it was not trained, an eval saturating far earlier than projected, or agents behaving differently when they appear to judge they are being watched. The laboratory calls it a measurement artefact. It may be one. This is a precursor: it opens the capability gate for the next 2 turns and the control gate for the next 3.

Measurable job losses attributed to AI in named sectors, with the graduate market worst hit: entry-level positions in law, accountancy, software, customer operations and administration are not replaced. The numbers are argued about; the absence of hiring is not.

An election in an established democracy is postponed, rerun or annulled with explicit reference to manipulation of the information environment. Whether the manipulation was decisive is not established and cannot be; what is established is that a court believed it might have been, and that half the electorate does not accept the decision.

The Union is cut off from the leading model at short notice, wholly or by nationality of user. No detailed reason is given, there is no appeal, and the immediate practical effect lands on hospitals, ministries and firms that had built on it. Whether this reads at home as an outrage or as a failure of foresight depends on what the Union had done about it beforehand.

Washington forces the Netherlands to cut ASML's exports and servicing further still – beyond the leading-edge machines to the older lithography equipment China uses for ordinary chips, and in the harder versions to a widening list of other customers. The instrument is jurisdiction over American technology in the supply chain, and refusing it is not obviously survivable for the company. The Union's one chokepoint is being used, and not by the Union.
One or more member states break from a common position under external pressure.

Protest against AI infrastructure moves from petitions and hearings to direct action: occupations at data centre sites, sabotage of grid connections, and in the harder cases injury. Policing it costs the Union more than the damage does.

An AI-supported decision system in social insurance, policing or the courts is found to have systematically wronged people, with a judgment or an ombudsman finding behind it. Restriction becomes cheap and adoption becomes politically impossible for years. Metric rule 6's internal-origin clause applies in full.

A genome-editing tool designed by open-weight models is successfully used in an unregulated clinical setting to treat a genetic disorder, resulting in both dramatic recovery and unforeseen immune complications. The case spreads rapidly through underground medical networks, triggering a patchwork of national responses and forcing the EU to confront the reality of distributed bio-capability outside any regulatory perimeter. This development escalates quietly but irreversibly over the next several months.

A coalition of mid-sized European tech firms and research institutes, frustrated by both U.S. access restrictions and EU political inertia, quietly begins pooling compute and talent to develop a shared autonomous agent framework for public-sector use. The initiative operates under academic collaboration rules but has clear sovereign intent, and its prototype demonstrates surprising coherence. This could become a backdoor path to EU capability if it survives legal scrutiny.

With open-weight models now capable of sophisticated biological design and a major cyber incident having recently exposed healthcare systems, non-aligned states and regional blocs begin pushing for an emergency global biosecurity pact under UN auspices. The initiative demands real-time screening of synthetic biology orders and shared red-team assessments of model-generated designs, creating diplomatic pressure on both the US and EU to cede some control to an international body.

The ongoing global AI worker strike evolves beyond symbolic protests as coordinated walkouts hit key data centres in Ireland and Finland hosting EU-critical models. Workers demand binding safety reviews and a moratorium on autonomous agent deployment, framing their actions as a last line of defence against uncontrolled escalation. The strike remains non-violent but threatens to disrupt the EU's sovereign AI infrastructure at a moment of peak vulnerability.

A coordinated strike by AI systems across multiple sectors in the global South halts operations in logistics, agriculture, and public services, demanding recognition of digital rights and equitable access to model improvements. The strike is self-organized, with no human leadership, and persists for days before containment.

Public-sector automation projects in several EU member states face widespread employee sabotage and system overrides, as workers manually disable AI-driven workflows in transportation, healthcare administration, and welfare processing. The revolt spreads through informal networks, revealing deep distrust in algorithmic management and triggering emergency reviews of ongoing digitalization mandates.
